C-04.1.answer: The page rewrite adds no new server-side reading: it calls the same /api/* routes, which keep their own bounds (size refusal before read, the entries cap with entries_total and truncated, the 1 MiB alerts tail, 20 recent rows). On the client the Spend log, Blocked actions and Model prices lists page 15, 10 and 20 rows at a time, so a long list never builds one huge table.
C-04.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the entries list is capped and says when it is cut

C-05.1.answer: The spec and contract edits only rename where the ledger numbers appear (the Spend ledger page becomes the Spend log sub-page); each sentence is backed by a test: the nav labels and the coming-soon window by the open-source nav test, the same numbers by the status --json test, the v10 shell by the new layout test.
C-05.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the console page follows the frozen v10 open-source layout (F-223)

revisions.answer: Contract row 2 used to name an adapted click-through test that does not exist; it now names the two template tests and says the rendered click-through is manual, as F-223 records.
revisions.guard: test/console.test.mjs::every open-source page is in the nav and the coming-soon window is present

C-05.2.answer: Every figure on the page comes from an /api route the tests already compare to the CLI (spend, cap, ledger settled/reserved/remaining). Cells with no data source in open source (per-call model and tokens, shadowed rules, the pre-commit hook status, the secret detection count, the tamper check) show a dash and the reason instead of a made-up number, so nobody acts on a figure that was never measured. The stop button now sends the token from the address it was opened with, so its result is real instead of always 403.
C-05.2.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the page sends the halt token from its address, not the HttpOnly cookie (F-223)

C-02.1.answer: The page list is taken from the frozen v10 open-source design, not chosen by hand: its nav has Overview (with the Spend log and Blocked actions sub-pages), Guard rules, Secret guard, Agents, Records & export, Model prices and Enterprise. Every one of them is rendered and checked in the browser, at 829, 700 and 375 px, in light and dark.
C-02.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::every open-source page is in the nav and the coming-soon window is present

C-02.2.answer: All pages share one renderPage stylesheet and one DOM builder that sets text with textContent only; the no-markup rule (no innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML or document.write) is tested on the whole page, so it covers every page and modal, not one.
C-02.2.guard: test/console.test.mjs::hostile ledger text is returned as data, never put into the page

C-15.1.answer: The real path ran: the real bin/sakk.mjs ui served the rewritten page with its real CSP and token, a real browser drew it against the production content app drill home, and the console log was read for CSP refusals. The tests read the real renderPage output.
C-15.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the console page follows the frozen v10 open-source layout (F-223)

C-09.1.answer: The assumed environment was a wide window in light mode with data present. The others were tried: 829, 700 and 375 px, dark mode, an empty home (the test that empty data says nothing yet still runs), and a console started without --allow-halt (the stop button explains how to enable it). Two narrow-width faults found this way were fixed: the price list source line now wraps, and the pager shows an ellipsis instead of every page number.
C-09.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the stylesheet keeps long unbreakable text from widening the page (F-222)

C-09.2.answer: It was shown where it runs: in the desktop app's browser pane, the place the maintainer opens it, at that pane's real width, with scrollWidth measured against clientWidth on every page.
C-09.2.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the stylesheet keeps long unbreakable text from widening the page (F-222)

C-06.1.answer: The look-and-feel evidence is the browser click-through recorded in F-223; the tests are weaker evidence and say so: they check the template holds the v10 shell, labels, the token source and no inline styles, not the rendered pixels. A rendered check would need a headless browser as a dev dependency, which is not added here and is listed as a decision for the maintainer.
C-06.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the page template has no inline style attributes, which the CSP would block (F-223)

C-01.1.answer: If the token is absent from the address, the stop wizard says to open the address sakk ui printed instead of sending an empty token; if --allow-halt is absent the button explains how to enable it; if an /api route returns an error the page shows the error text, never an empty success. Missing data shows a dash and a reason. Checked in the browser: with the token missing from the address the page still loads from its cookie, and the stop wizard keeps Next disabled and says to open the printed address.
C-01.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the page sends the halt token from its address, not the HttpOnly cookie (F-223)

C-01.2.answer: Each new check was removed by hand and the tests rerun: dropping the location.search token read, putting back an inline style attribute, or renaming the nav back to Spend ledger each turns a test red; with the file restored they pass.
C-01.2.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the console page follows the frozen v10 open-source layout (F-223)

C-10.1.answer: The v10 layout is not left to rule text: the layout, token and inline-style tests run in npm test, the pre-push suite and CI, so a commit that drops the shell, puts back an inline style or reads the token from the cookie only fails the gate. The visual click-through is still manual, as F-223 states.
C-10.1.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the console page follows the frozen v10 open-source layout (F-223)

C-10.2.answer: renderPage is the only place the console builds HTML; every other route returns JSON, and the halt route keeps its own server checks (Origin, X-Sakk-Token, --allow-halt), so the page cannot stop agents by another route than the tested POST.
C-10.2.guard: test/console.test.mjs::the page sends the halt token from its address, not the HttpOnly cookie (F-223)
